title: 考研英语二2011年真题及答案解析（整卷）

sentences.text: Outside directors are supposed to serve as helpful, yet less biased, advisers on a firm's board.
sentences.translation: 外部董事应当在公司董事会中充当有益但较少偏见的顾问。由于他们的财富和声誉是在其他地方建立的，他们大概有足够的独立性来反对首席执行官的提议。如果股价和天空一起下跌，外部董事应该能够基于自己经历过的危机提供建议。

sentences.text: Having made their wealth and their reputations elsewhere, they presumably have enough independence to disagree with the chief executive's proposals.
If the sky and the share price are falling, outside directors should be able to give advice based on having weathered their own crises.
The researchers from Ohio University used a database that covered more than 10,000 firms and more than 64,000 different directors between 1989 and 2004.
sentences.translation: 懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2011-english-two/section2-part-a-1/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好found that after a surprise departure, the probability that the company will subsequently have to restateearnings increases by nearly 20%. The likelihood of being named in a federal class-action lawsuit alsoincreases, and the stock is likely to perform worse. The effect tended to be larger for larger firms.Although a correlation between them leaving and subsequent bad performance at the firm is suggestive,it does not mean that such directors are always jumping off a sinking ship. Often they "trade up,"leaving riskier, smaller firms for larger and more stable firms.Ohio University的研究人员使用了一个涵盖1989年至2004年间超过10,000家公司和超过64,000名不同董事的数据库。然后他们只是简单地检查哪些董事从一份委托声明留任到下一份。离开董事会最可能的原因是年龄，因此研究人员将注意力集中在70岁以下董事的那些"意外"离职上。他们发现，在意外离职后，公司随后必须重述收益的概率增加了近20%。被列入联邦集体诉讼的可能性也会增加，股票表现可能会更差。这种影响对于规模更大的公司往往更明显。尽管他们离职与公司随后的糟糕表现之间的相关性具有暗示性，但这并不意味着这些董事总是在弃船逃跑。他们往往是"向上跳槽"，离开风险较高的小公司，转投规模更大、更稳定的公司。

sentences.text: Then they simply checked which directors stayed from one proxy statement to the next.
The most likely reason for departing a board was age, so the researchers concentrated on those "surprise" disappearances by directors under the age of 70.

But the researchers believe that outside directors have an easier time of avoiding a blow to their reputations if they leave a firm before bad news breaks, even if a review of history shows they were on the board at the time any wrongdoing occurred.
sentences.translation: 但研究人员认为，如果外部董事在坏消息曝光之前离开公司，他们更容易避免声誉受损，即使历史回顾显示在任何不当行为发生时他们就在董事会任职。希望在困难时期留住外部董事的公司可能必须创造激励措施。否则，外部董事将效仿Simmons女士的做法，再次在校园里大受欢迎。

sentences.text: Firms who want to keep their outside directors through tough times may have to create incentives.
Otherwise outside directors will follow the example of Ms. Simmons, once again very popular on campus.
It has not been much fun.
sentences.translation: 懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2011-english-two/section2-part-a-2/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好suburbs. Yet these desperate measures have proved the right ones and, sadly for many journalists, theycan be pushed further.这个过程并不怎么愉快。许多报纸通过把记者推下船来维持生存。美国新闻编辑协会估计,自2007年以来已经失去了13500个新闻编辑室的工作岗位。读者正在为更薄的产品支付更多费用。一些报纸甚至敢于拒绝向偏远郊区投递。然而这些绝望的措施被证明是正确的,而且令许多记者遗憾的是,这些措施还可以进一步推行。

sentences.text: Many papers stayed afloat by pushing journalists overboard.
The American Society of News Editors reckons that 13,500 newsroom jobs have gone since 2007.
Readers are paying more for slimmer products.
Some papers even had the nerve to refuse delivery to distant
The whirlwind that swept through newsrooms harmed everybody, but much of the damage has been concentrated in areas where newspapers are least distinctive.
sentences.translation: 席卷新闻编辑室的旋风伤害了所有人,但大部分损害集中在报纸最不具特色的领域。汽车和电影评论员已经消失了。科学和综合商业记者也是如此。驻外记者站被大幅削减。报纸因此变得不那么完整了。但完整性在报业中不再是一种美德。

sentences.text: Car and film reviewers have gone.
So have science and general business reporters.
Foreign bureaus have been savagely cut off.
Newspapers are less complete as a result.
But completeness is no longer a virtue in the newspaper business.

We tend to think of the decades immediately following World War II as a time of prosperity and growth, with soldiers returning home by the millions, going off to college on the G. I. Bill and lining up at the marriage bureaus.
sentences.translation: 我们倾向于认为二战后的几十年是一个繁荣和增长的时期，数百万士兵返回家园，依靠《退伍军人权利法案》上大学，并在婚姻登记处排队。

sentences.text: But when it came to their houses, it was a time of common sense and a belief that less could truly be more.
sentences.translation: 但就住房而言,那是一个崇尚常识、相信少即是多的时代。在大萧条和战争期间,美国人学会了简朴生活,这种克制与战后对未来的信心相结合,使小型高效住宅成为一种时尚。

sentences.text: During the Depression and the war, Americans had learned to live with less, and that restraint, in combination with the postwar confidence in the future, made small, efficient housing positively stylish.
Economic condition was only a stimulus for the trend toward efficient living.
sentences.translation: 经济状况只是高效生活趋势的一个刺激因素。"少即是多"这句话实际上最早是由一位德国人、建筑师Ludwig Mies van der Rohe推广的,他像其他与包豪斯设计学院有关的人一样,在二战前移民到美国并在美国建筑学院任职。这些设计师对美国建筑的发展产生了巨大影响,但没有人比Mies的影响更大。懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2011-english-two/section2-part-a-3/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好

sentences.text: The phrase "less is more" was actually first popularized by a German, the architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, who like other people associated with the Bauhaus, a school of design, emigrated to the United States before World War II and took up posts at American architecture schools.
These designers came to exert enormous influence on the course of American architecture, but none more so than Mies.
As well as those chronic problems, the EU faces an acute crisis in its economic core, the 16 countries that use the single currency.
sentences.translation: 除了这些长期问题，欧盟在其经济核心——使用单一货币的16个国家——还面临着一场严重危机。市场已不再相信欧元区经济体，无论强弱，会因共享单一货币的约束而终有一天趋于一致，而单一货币使缺乏竞争力的成员国无法采取货币贬值这一权宜之计。

sentences.text: Markets have lost faith that the euro zone's economies, weaker or stronger, will one day converge thanks to the discipline of sharing a single currency, which denies uncompetitive members the quick fix of devaluation.
Yet the debate about how to save Europe's single currency from disintegration is stuck.
sentences.translation: 然而，关于如何拯救欧洲单一货币免于分崩离析的辩论陷入了僵局。之所以陷入僵局,是因为欧元区的主导力量法国和德国在欧元区内需要加强协调一致方面意见相同，但在协调什么方面存在分歧。

sentences.text: It is stuck because the euro zone's dominant powers, France and Germany, agree on the need for greater harmonisation within the euro zone, but disagree about what to harmonise.
Germany thinks the euro must be saved by stricter rules on borrowing, spending and competitiveness, backed by quasi-automatic sanctions for governments that do not obey.
sentences.translation: 懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2011-english-two/section2-part-a-4/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好a country's voting rights in EU ministerial councils. It insists that economic co-ordination should involveall 27 members of the EU club, among whom there is a small majority for free-market liberalism andeconomic rigour; in the inner core alone, Germany fears, a small majority favour French interference.德国认为必须通过更严格的借贷、支出和竞争力规则来拯救欧元，并对不遵守的政府实施准自动制裁。这些制裁可能包括威胁冻结面向贫困地区的欧盟基金和欧盟大型项目，甚至暂停一国在欧盟部长理事会中的投票权。德国坚持认为经济协调应涉及欧盟俱乐部的全部27个成员国，其中支持自由市场自由主义和经济严谨的占微弱多数；德国担心，仅在核心圈内，支持法国式干预的会占微弱多数。

sentences.text: These might include threats to freeze EU funds for poorer regions and EU mega-projects, and even the suspension of
A "southern" camp headed by France wants something different: "European economic government" within an inner core of euro-zone members.
sentences.translation: 以法国为首的"南方"阵营想要的是不同的东西：在欧元区成员国核心圈内建立"欧洲经济政府"。换句话说，这意味着政治家干预货币政策，以及通过共同欧洲债券或完全的财政转移支付来降低政府借贷成本，从而建立一个从富裕成员国向贫困成员国再分配的体系。最后，接近法国政府的人士私下表示，欧元区成员国应就某些财政和社会协调达成一致：例如，限制企业税率或劳动力成本方面的竞争。

sentences.text: Translated, that means politicians intervening in monetary policy and a system of redistribution from richer to poorer members, via cheaper borrowing for governments through common Eurobonds or complete fiscal transfers.
Finally, figures close to the French government have murmured, euro-zone members should agree to some fiscal and social harmonisation:
e.g., curbing competition in corporate-tax rates or labour costs.
It is too soon to write off the EU.
sentences.translation: 现在就对欧盟下定论还为时过早。它仍然是世界上最大的贸易集团。在最好的状态下，欧洲计划是非常自由的：围绕一个由27个富国和穷国组成的单一市场建立，其内部边界对商品、资本和劳动力的开放程度远超任何可比的贸易区。这是一次雄心勃勃的尝试，旨在削弱全球化最尖锐的锋芒，使资本主义变得温和。

sentences.text: It remains the world's largest trading block.

At its best, the European project is remarkably liberal: built around a single market of 27 rich and poor countries, its internal borders are far more open to goods, capital and labour than any comparable trading area.
It is an ambitious attempt to blunt the sharpest edges of globalisation, and make capitalism benign.
Many everyday tasks take a surprising toll on the environment.

sentences.text: A Google search can leak between 0.2 and 7.0 grams of CO2, depending on how many attempts are needed to get the "right" answer.
To deliver results to its users quickly, then, Google has to maintain vast data centres around the world, packed with powerful computers.
While producing large quantities of CO2, these computers emit a great deal of heat, so the centres need to be well air-conditioned, which uses even more energy.
P3 However, Google and other big tech providers monitor their efficiency closely and make improvements.
Monitoring is the first step on the road to reduction, but there is much more to be done, and not just by big companies.
